newsitem.title: USA: Cook County, Ill., adopts bad debt writeoff plan.
newsitem.headline: Cook County, Ill., adopts bad debt writeoff plan.

text.p: Cook County commissioners adopted a policy Tuesday to write off bad debts accumulated at its public health facilities in Chicago and surrounding areas, a spokesman said.
The new policy will allow Cook County to close the books on an estimated $1.036 billion of uncollectable debts amassed by patients at its public hospital in Chicago from 1975 to 1992.
Patients have accumulated another $270 million of debts for services rendered since 1992 as well.
Under the policy, the Bureau of Health Services will be permitted to clear the books once all efforts have been exhausted.
